title: DuckDB has no second engine: a streamed result equals the materialised one
verdict: no fallback; nothing to record beyond the equality of the two result modes
description: DuckDB runs every operator in its one vectorised, push-based pipeline executor; there is no in-memory engine that a streaming one hands operators to (as Polars's streaming engine does, polars-exec-streaming-fallback). Reading a result as a stream of record batches (`to_arrow_reader(1000)`) gives the same rows as `fetchall()` for a grouped aggregate, a window, a join and a sort with a limit, over 300,000 rows.
reference: The reference has no engines; sverify runs DuckDB through its own materialised and streamed readers alike.

evidence.sql: CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT i, (i*7919)%1000 AS k, (i%13)::DOUBLE/7 AS x FROM range(300000) r(i); each of GROUP BY k with sum(x), row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY k ORDER BY x, i), a self-join on k, ORDER BY x DESC, i LIMIT 50000, read with con.execute(q).fetchall() and con.execute(q).to_arrow_reader(1000).read_all()
evidence.observed: rows equal in all four queries (1000, 300000, 10 and 50000 rows)

provenance.notes: Source reading of the executor was not done: the claim of no fallback rests on the engine's documented single pipeline executor and the equality above.
